note: Re-judged 2026-10-24 (independent auditor, authored none of the change). RFC 8277 Section 2.4: "Upon reception, the value of the Compatibility field MUST be ignored." 238bdb62e9 (spec-refuse-instead-of-defaulting) changed PeerInfo/StructuredEvent PeerAS from uint32 to rpc.RemoteAS; the unit now writes rpc.RemoteASOf(N) where it wrote N, the same known peer AS, and no assertion, input byte or expected value changed (TestVPNWithdrawalJSONConsumersIgnoreCompatibility, both tags). The re-stamp inside 238bdb62e9 does not match the unit at HEAD; this judgement re-reads it. Verdict unchanged: enforced. Earlier judgement follows. RFC 8277 Section 2.4, rfc/full/rfc8277.txt:623-692: "Upon reception, the value of the Compatibility field MUST be ignored." Independently read all 18 distinct tagged functions (29 tag units) across format, rib, rr, rs, server and plugin/ipc, including the RIB compatibilityRouteState/compatibilityVPNPromotion helpers. Recommended 0x800000 and distinct zero, S-set, arbitrary S-clear and all-ones inputs preserve exact prefix/RD/ADD-PATH zero-or-17 identities, without labels, through real registered JSON and RPC decoders. RIB fixtures assert exact surviving native routes and exact Withdraw versus replacement Update, including the other PE's next hop and original label/path. RR/RS fixtures assert exact inventories, then exact sorted peer-down native commands and reparsed survivor NLRIs. These are separate input cases with consequence assertions, not duplicate polarities on one no-error assertion. Read all five retained producer guards: Withdraw/LabeledWithdrawnPrefix choose withdrawal framing, wrapNLRI ignores Compatibility before CIDR decoding while retaining negotiated identifiers, appendNLRIJSONValue passes withdrawal context and excludes INET from the label decoder, and sendBatchedWithdrawals preserves retained native bytes plus ADD-PATH framing and calls recoverRouteSel. Its command-hook carrier proves command construction, not downstream recipient delivery; that latter behavior is not claimed here. Implemented-tested for this receipt/identity requirement; no absent feature found in this scope, and no newly observed runtime or mutant result. Preserve every existing code guard. Rejudged 2026-10-23 (refuse-instead-of-defaulting F3) after appendNLRIJSONValue changed: presence of the Path Identifier is now nlri.HasPathID(n) alone, and the bare-prefix branch tests !addPath instead of !addPath && n.PathID() == 0. RFC 8277 Section 2.4, rfc/full/rfc8277.txt:643: "Upon reception, the value of the Compatibility field MUST be ignored." The guard's role for this requirement is unchanged: withdraw is still passed to the registry decoder and an *nlri.INET is still never handed to the label decoder. The labeled withdrawal reaches it as an INET that wireu.wrapNLRI builds with nlri.ParseINET(..., hasAddPath), so presence follows the session negotiation: identifiers 0 and 17 under ADD-PATH still print path-id, and without ADD-PATH the identifier was and is absent. The only output that changed is an in-process prefix NLRI holding a nonzero identifier it does not carry, which no tagged unit of this requirement produces. All tagged units re-run green 2026-10-23 (format, rib, rr, rs, server, plugin/ipc). Verdict stands. Re-read again 2026-10-23 over the function as it now stands, which also carries a concurrent refuse-instead-of-defaulting F2 change: a plugin family decoder's refusal and an opaque WireNLRI that names no route are now written as an undecoded element (appendUndecodedNLRIJSON) instead of falling through to a route-shaped value. That branch runs only when the decoder refuses; every tagged unit asserts the decoder reads the withdrawal for each Compatibility value (0x800000, zero, S-set, S-clear, all-ones), and the INET exclusion and the withdraw context are unchanged, so the receipt behaviour judged here did not change. Units re-run green over this version. Verdict stands.
